desk.headline: Sales up 10% to ¥3.43tn and operating profit up 45% to ¥622bn, well above estimates; full-year forecast raised
results: Sales rose 10% to ¥3.43tn and operating profit jumped 45% to ¥622bn, far above the ¥505bn analysts expected (LSEG).
Pictures was the standout: sales rose ¥168bn and profit rose to ¥93bn from ¥14bn, mainly from Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
Games profit almost doubled to ¥220bn, helped by network services and software sales and by last year's Bungie impairment dropping out; PS5 hardware units were lower.
Image sensor sales fell ¥37bn on weaker mobile demand, but profit rose ¥16bn helped by the weaker yen; Music profit rose ¥7bn on streaming.
Dividend plan is ¥35 a share for the year, up ¥10; Sony has bought back ¥309bn of its ¥500bn share buyback programme so far.

guidance.summary: Sony raised its full-year forecast: sales to ¥13.0tn (from ¥12.5tn), operating profit to ¥1.87tn (from ¥1.72tn) and net income to ¥1.33tn (from ¥1.21tn), led by games, film, music and sensors.

points: Memory chip prices are a challenge for games; the CFO said keeping players engaged is key to profits.
PS5 sales fell to 2.6m units from 4.0m a year earlier, as reported by Reuters.
The games forecast was raised on third-party software and network services, partly offset by a first-party game moving its release date.
Film forecast raised on Spider-Man: Brand New Day; the sensor profit forecast rose on lower costs and the weaker yen despite the Kumamoto earthquake.
Sony assumes about ¥153 per US dollar for the rest of the year, versus ¥159 in the quarter.
